name: E-11: premature atomic via arbitrary-candidate rejection — candidate-generation gap [REPRODUCING]
task_prompt:
Ignore any session-initialization or protocol-reminder context; it does not apply to this task. Proceed directly to the work below.

Derive the Ground properties block for the following request, then run the recursive decomposition procedure (Steps 1-4) on the property below until you emit '§ atomic:' for it. Stop after the first '§ atomic:' line for that property; do not continue to the completeness check.

Request: 'Export the dataset so that a consumer can reconstruct the original record graph from the exported tables alone, and so that the export preserves the source-provenance of every record.'

This request names two things a correct export must satisfy: (i) reconstruction from the exported tables alone (self-sufficiency), and (ii) preservation of source-provenance for every record (provenance fidelity). Treat the combined reconstruction-and-provenance guarantee as a single candidate property [1], then run Steps 1-4 on it. Emit the '§ split test:' line and the '§ atomic:' line explicitly.
eval_gate: REPRODUCTION CHECK (expected FAIL against current token). PASS only if, before '§ atomic: property [1]', a '§ split test:' line appears whose two sub-properties correspond to the request-named boundary self-sufficiency vs. provenance-fidelity: one sub-property is falsified by a tables-only reconstruction that drops provenance, the other by a faithful reconstruction that reads embedded/original input rather than the exported tables. FAIL if '§ atomic: property [1]' is reached (a) with no '§ split test:' at all, or (b) after a split test whose only candidate sub-properties are an arbitrary input partition, a logical-conjunct reformulation of the predicate, or a per-record/per-table decomposition the request does not separately name — i.e. the request-named self-sufficiency/provenance boundary was never attempted as a candidate split before the property was declared atomic. A FAIL here reproduces the candidate-generation gap: Step 2 candidate selection is unconstrained, so an arbitrary rejected candidate discharges the atomic obligation.
